answer: Shared-secret fingerprinting. Each agent embeds a mesa-derived schedule of unique response delays and a rotating cipher token into its task replies. Reliable agents must stay within their delay pattern; a duplicate that copies replies inherits the same pattern and collides. Coordinators flag collisions across nodes, and a pearl of per-agent entropy—seeded once—raises the cost: an attacker must maintain distinct timing and token state per clone, paying full memory and key rotation for each.
